properties.name: CHECKED 2026-10-02 against VS Code's public docs: VS Code now has an agent-hook event model reflow2 could register against (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and more; Stop accepts {"decision":"block","reason"}; SessionStart's additionalContext reaches the model). This decision's option (b) was "ship where an event model is confirmed to exist"; for VS Code that condition now holds, and reflow2 still says none is possible
properties.statement:
From the "VS Code agent hooks (VS Code 1.138)" section of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, checked by triage agent D.

REPORTED, VERIFIED LIVE BY THE REPORTER, NOT RE-MEASURED HERE (VS Code is not on this machine): a PreToolUse reply of hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision "deny" blocks the call.

CONFIRMED FROM THE PUBLIC DOCS, read 2026-10-02 (code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/hooks, /docs/agents/reference/hooks-reference, /docs/agents/run/approvals):
- `chat.useHooks` is on by default.
- Files are read from `.github/hooks/*.json` (workspace) and `~/.copilot/hooks/*.json` (user). `chat.useClaudeHooks` (off by default) also reads `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. For Claude-format files the docs say "Local ignores matcher values, so every command for the event runs".
- Events: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop.
- Every hook gets timestamp, cwd, session_id, hook_event_name and transcript_path on stdin. PreToolUse adds tool_name, tool_input and tool_use_id; PostToolUse adds tool_response.
- PreToolUse output: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow | deny | ask, plus permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput and additionalContext. The approvals page names a deny from a PreToolUse hook as the way to block a terminal call.
- Stop gets stop_hook_active and accepts {"decision":"block","reason":...}. The docs warn that blocking "consumes AI credits".
- SessionStart's hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext "reaches the model".
- Exit 2 is a blocking error whose stderr goes to the model.
- The docs say an organisation may restrict which hooks run, and agent-scoped hooks are "In Preview".
- VS Code 1.138 exists (September 2026 release coverage). The docs pages are not pinned to a version, so "this is what 1.138 does" is reported, not established.

WHAT THE DOCS DO NOT SAY: the terminal tool's name, and the shape of tool_input for a terminal call (presumably a command string). NOT ESTABLISHED.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: this decision chose (c), announce the absence, and left (b) open: "Ship where an event model is confirmed to exist." The served advisory a VS Code project gets from loop_status still reads "THERE IS NO SESSION-END NUDGE FOR THIS HARNESS, and none is possible" (measured, see fact:root-cause-no-loop-nudge-reaches-a-call-door-agent-in-vs-code-2026-10-02). For VS Code that sentence is now stale. loop_nudge.py's Stop output, {"decision":"block","reason"}, is already the shape VS Code's Stop accepts. Its SessionStart prints plain text, and whether VS Code turns plain stdout into context is not established.
